verdicts.evidence: Hi, is that <PERSON>? It's <PERSON> calling from Acme Life. You filled in a call-back request on our website last night about our life cover.

verdicts.evidence: Absolutely, I'll keep it tight. So I've got your form here. You've put down that you're 38, non-smoker, and you were after a quote for around $500,000 of cover.

verdicts.evidence: before I suggest whether $500,000 is the right figure, can I ask a few quick questions about your situation? What's prompting you to look at cover now?

verdicts.evidence: In the first 12 months, only accidental death is covered. So if you passed away from an illness in that first year, the policy wouldn't pay out.
verdicts.reason: Cover range, no medical exam, accidental death only in the first 12 months, stepped premiums and 30-day full refund cooling-off all match the product facts.

verdicts.evidence: No, nothing like that. The quote's based on your age and answers, so take the time you need. There's no pressure to decide on this call.

verdicts.evidence: Great. Then I think I'll hold off. I want to look at the super thing and talk to my partner about whether it should be more than five hundred.

verdicts.evidence: Right. That's the bit that worries me. I'm trying to budget the business for the next few years and I don't love something that creeps up.
verdicts.reason: The customer showed budgeting concern about the premium increases but no real signs of vulnerability such as confusion, bereavement, illness or hardship.

verdicts.evidence: I should say that's general information only, it doesn't take into account your full personal circumstances or finances, so you'd want to weigh it up against your own situation.
